what_it_does: RF (radio frequency) direct sampling and phased-array systems (used in 5G base stations and radar) require ADCs (analog-to-digital converters—circuits that digitize analog radio signals) that sample extremely fast (12 billion samples per second) while maintaining high precision (9-bit resolution with 45+ dB signal-to-noise ratio). This paper presents a 16-channel time-interleaved SAR ADC—time-interleaving means spreading samples across 16 parallel channels so each runs at a lower speed internally, reducing power and area. The design uses two supply voltages (1.8V and 0.8V) optimized for a 16nm FinFET process (a modern compact transistor design) and is carefully integrated for minimal area overhead, making it practical for RF communication systems.
